## Chapter Twenty-Three

Total Recall



The next week went by agonizingly slow for Lucas as he spent his days going out and picking up list after list of equipment and then spent his evenings pitching in where he could to help setup the room for the end of the week where he would descend into the bed and experience events that had not happened for nearly a century as if he himself were there.

Lucas was excited and scared, as he watched Emma check and recheck the connections, his impatience building until he didn’t think he could take it anymore.

Then on the seventh day he awoke, springing to his feet, he was giddy with anticipation. The fear had come and settled in and like an old friend , it was familiar , now all that was left was the excitement of the experience. He hurriedly took a shower and dressed , making his way to the main room now dubbed Command and Control or the common room depending on who you asked. He ate with gusto that morning, Rolle coming in and nodding at him as he himself ate. “Are you ready?” he asked, eyeing his friend over some dry cereal and a glass of water. Lucas nodded with a mouthful of protein bar.

He would have told Rolle he had been ready since the beginning of the week, but his friend knew, they had sat up at night talking about this very thing every night since they had first discussed it. And now it was here. He couldn’t finish his breakfast fast enough. Once they were done both men policed the trash and headed for the scanner room as quickly as they could without running. Emma and Victoria were already there and from the look of it , had been there for a while, still going over connections and checking the newly built interface program that Victoria had been working on since Monday. As they made there way into the room Victoria looked at Lucas giving him a meaningful nod, telling him both welcome and that she was ready.

He stood back allowing Emma to finish, not pressuring her as he more than most wanted to ensure that the electronics all worked and there would be no failure, because a failure could mean a neural overload according to the small pixie of a woman and that would leave him in a coma, his brain struggling to comprehend what was real and wasn’t.

Finally, Emma stepped back, eying the machine and then locking eyes with Lucas she nodded once at him. The doctor entered soon after carrying a small bag and wheeling a tray full of instruments and electronics. She said her hello’s and wheeled the cart over to the vertical bed where she began to setup. Lucas was not sure what the items did, but he trusted the doc to ensure that he would come out alive. As she completed her setup, that old friend began to creep forward announcing himself as he felt real fear since earlier in the week. His heart rate quickened as did his breath and he fought to keep it under control. Locking eyes with the doctor he knew she could tell what he was thinking. She didn’t call him on it though and he appreciated that. Sally however was conspicuously not present this morning “Where is Sally?” Lucas whispered to Rolle who just shrugged.

“Sally has some other things to do so he won’t be joining us today, are you ready to get started?” Doc asked gently. Lucas nodded and walked over to the bed, breathing slowly to keep his heart under control. Every warning echoing through his head as he eyed the machine, the bed now looking like more like a torture device then an instrument of medicine. But he swallowed the fear and doubt. He had agreed to this, looked forward to it, he couldn’t back out now. The Doc and Emma helped him up onto the bed, strapping him in. He almost panicked with the first strap went across his chest, locking him to the bed. But again, he suppressed it, doing his best to bury the fear.

Once he was strapped in, Emma held a curved bar, it was like a sliver of helmet, the curve in the shape of his hear. The inside of it glowed and coalesced with blue light. Emma gently put it behind his head, locking it into a base of some kind. It never actually touched his head, but where the blue light shined, he could feel a slight heat on his scalp. “Just relax, we are almost ready” she whispered to him putting a reassuring hand on his shoulder.

The doctor rummaged in her bag for a moment and then pulled out a metal ball, about the size of a baseball and put it in Lucas’s palm. “Squeeze it” she said, and he did without even thinking, A tingling pain shot up his arm and he almost dropped the ball, the doc putting her hand over his to ensure it stayed there.

She got his attention , held eye contact “This is important, as you are in there, your brain will be receiving sensory input from the machine, this might be confusing, remember you are only along for the ride, you are not this person, when you start to forget or doubt that, squeeze your hand. This will send a small pain up your arm, giving your mind actual input it can focus on to remember that you are here, and not actually there” She finished. Waiting for Lucas to nod, to let her know he understood. “Do not drop the ball, do not forget that you are only a spectator there” she continued, never leaving eye contact with Lucas.

“Okay, let’s do this” he said with as much false bravado as he could muster. The Doc went around the room getting verbal confirmation that everyone was ready. “Okay, here we go” and before Lucas could protest, a white light filled his vision, his body feeling like it was falling from a high distance, he didn’t know if he screamed, he thought he did, and then the world went black.



He opened his eyes, reaching up and feeling the odd sensor against his skull, it itched, but the doctor had assured him, get he would get used to it. Why did I ever agree to allow them to use me as a damn guinea pig he thought, shaking his head as the mental answer came as quickly because you lead by example dumb ass and Joe almost laughed out loud.

“Colonel, are you okay, does it hurt, we can adjust it if you need us to” Henry asked. Captain Henry Douglas had been Joe’s friend and the complex’s Senior medical doctor going on a decade, this had been his pet project for most of that time. “No Joe, your little toy is fine” Joe teased, seeing Henry wince with irritation.

Henry was a short man, balding with thick glasses, and over the years his waistline had grown, good living and a happy marriage contributing to the paunch he now sported. His white lab coat was usually self consciously buttoned to cover it, as it was today. He took off his glasses and cleaned then with the end of the coat. Joe knew his friend well enough to know it was a stall tactic allowing him to collect his thoughts. “Now joe, you can’t take it off, it will be on you for the next thirty days, no matter what” Henry said seriously. Joe nodded with impatient irritation, he had work to do , and besides he had signed the form, gotten the riot act from his commanding officer who had made that stipulation an order, meaning if Joe did take it off, he could be court martialed, and he wasn’t about to give anyone the excuse to do that to him.

“I know Henry, are we done here?” he asked his friend impatiently. Henry shook his head “Yes Joe, but please, be careful with that, it’s still in early development stages, don’t go banging it around.

Joe nodded and got up from bed. As he rose, he looked down at his much shorter friend. Unlike the Doc he had not gained much weight in the last decade, still maintaining the waistline of a young recruit, probably due to his divorce, besides Beth couldn’t cook while they were married for crap. He thought a small smile gracing his features. I don’t miss that at all Joe’s thought finished. Wait, I or he? Lucas thought, his mind trying to resolve the experience of being in Joe’s body. But I am not in his body Lucas thought, the room around him seemed to flash and then go dark, finally returning to normal as his mind rebelled against the sensor input. Lucas squeezed the ball the pain shooting up his arm, seemed to clear his view. Anchor him as now he understood, he could feel his relatives’ thoughts, as if they were his own, thoughts about his great grandmother that he wasn’t sure he wanted to know. But it was too late now, he was in the thick of it.

Lucas mentally settled in allowing the thoughts to cascade over his mind as Joe moved towards the door of the all too familiar room. It was the same but different he noticed and then Lucas, not Joe mentally rolled his eyes. Its seventy years newer he chided himself and then quieted and concentrated on Joe and Joe’s experiences.

Joe exited the room, still itching at the two sensor modules on his temple, damn these are irritating he thought, remembering what the doctor said, he would get used to them within a day or two. He rolled his eyes, ensuring no one was around to see it. He didn’t know if he could last a day or two, this was going to drive him crazy long before that. “Colonel” came a familiar voice from behind him. The heavy New York accent a dead giveaway for his executive officer “Hey Sal, what’s the sit rep” Joe asked, giving his partner the short hand for “Situation Report”. Sal was as tall as joe, but stockier, he was the walking embodiment of the New York Italian stereo type, he tended to strut like a peacock rather then walk and it was something that always amused Joe about him.

“We are green across the board” Sal said, the last word sounding more like “bawd”. Joe nodded “Okay, get some rack time, I will take next shift, Tell Ming she can stand down, I don’t think I am going to rest until I get used to these damn things, so there is no sense in both of us losing sleep” he said, pointing at the modules. Sal looked at them and made a face “I can’t believe you agreed to let Henry put those on you” he said and then swallowed a laugh, Joe and he were friends, but Joe was still his Commanding Officer, there was nothing to be gained by mocking him.

Joe nodded “You know me” he simply said. Sal smiled “Oh I do “he finished and walked away to find Ming. Joe continued on, Lucas recognizing the halls and rooms as his host, as he thought about him as host, passed through towards the command and control. Lucas rode along the conscious mind of his great grandfather marveling at the realism, he could feel his feet within the shoes and the cold air conditioning as he walked by the vent. But he wasn’t in control of where he was going. Reflecting on it, it would be easy for him to adopt his host’s objectives, meaning if his host wanted to go to the bathroom, then Lucas would feel the sensory input that would make his bladder feel heavy, meaning he would also want to go to the rest room. This would mean even though the host was in control of where the body went, he would also want to go so therefore he could easily forget that he wasn’t the one telling the body to walk there. Lucas squeezed the ball again sending the slight electric shock up his arm.

Reminding him that this was not his body, his body was lying up in a bed viewing this, using his brain to translate the sensory data into a coherent stream of information. The experience was surreal at the best of times, but the thought of what would happen should he lose his way, should his brain forget that this wasn’t his body, out of reflex he squeezed the ball again, almost like a security blanket.

The view of the command and control in its heyday swept across his mental view as Joe surveyed the soldiers all busy at work. It was almost a religious experience to see this place as it was meant to be, not the old husk of itself. Thirty soldiers swept around the room with early versions of Holo viewers over every desk as they monitored maps, data and intercepts. In the center of the controlled chaos stood the large viewing table, now showing a holo image of the planet along with what looked like satellites and telemetry data for each. Lucas wasn’t sure what he was looking at, but he thought it was the old US monitoring system.

It was a long way from the complete coverage New America had with Cerberus, but it was still nothing to scoff at. Lucas settled in to let the day play out as he observed, learning all he could about the complex and his great-grandfather.

Joe stepped into the large room, breathing in the chaos that surrounded him. His people were hard at work. “Bobby, I need the latest on coverage, do you have the report?” Joe called out. He enjoyed his command here, he was determined to keep it low key, he refused to call people by rank and chided them when they did it to him. Each one of these soldiers were at the top of their game and shouldn’t be looked down upon because they had a lower rank, he used first names and not last names, he knew every person all 342 people by name.

Bobby Ramirez walked over smiling, he handed a tablet to his boss. “We are looking at 73% coverage globally, we only have two satellites down right now, one is set to replace next month the other looks like a software glitch and the guys at JPL are working on it now” he finished , Joe couldn’t help but smile back, that was the best global coverage they have had to date, that gave them more ability to launch drones and collect SIGINT , Signals intelligence data than ever before. “Good, I have to jump on a call with DC here in a bit, they will enjoy that” he finished, and Bobby Ramirez walked away, intercepting one of his staff along the way.

Joe continued to his officer tablet in hand and calling out names and greetings along the way.

This bunker had been created initially during the cold war as a haven to allow his unit the ability to keep functioning even after a nuclear disaster. After 9-11 the bunker was overhauled, and his division was moved into it permanently they did thirty days on and then thirty days off giving full coverage out of the facility. He was the United States best kept secret, they had the latest technology, the top of the line people and the ability to deliver information that no one else could gain access to. The complex at Fort Meade and in Australia were awesome at intercept but he had the tools and computers to analyze that data in Realtime and get answers to the questions no one had even realized to ask yet.

The worst part of his job was dealing with the elected officials. It had seemed over the last two decades the candidates elected to president had gone downhill, this latest one, a business man who was not only pompous but reveled in his billionaire boys club status. His favorite phrase was “get it done”. He wasn’t smart enough to realize what that might entail for any given job, he just said it, Joe thought he did it to make himself feel like the big shot he thought he was.

He wasn’t sure what would happen if this trend continued, but it was bad enough where Joe was losing sleep more and more over the decisions of people who had jobs, they had no business doing. Grumbling he entered the office and closed the door.

He had come head to head with the current commander and chief more than once, the guy was a moron, who did not understand any of the capabilities they had for surveillance or intelligence gathering.

But then Joe hadn’t voted for the fucker. Sitting down he reviewed the coverage report and then dialed the secure number, as he waited six video windows sat blank awaiting their hosts. Within fifteen minutes heads began to appear and Joe recognized the face of the president, Secretary of State, Director of the CIA and FBI and Homeland all looking bored.

Joe settled in letting the CIA director take charge, it gave the little man an ego stroke and made him more manageable should Joe need more funding, which he always did. Distractedly he itched at the sensors, these things were going to irritate him all day he thought.

“Now before we get started, I have a couple of things to cover” Johnathan Marbury stated looking more like a disheveled accountant then the US Spymaster. Joe willed himself not to eyeroll and settled in to listen to the long-winded pain in the ass.

“We have had this monthly meeting going on eight years , in that time we have stopped numerous attacks and been able to manage a plethora of situations” He started, Joe recognized the tactic, he complimented before he came down on someone, Joe just hoped it wasn’t him this time.

Marbury leaned forward, putting his eyes into the camera and giving the impression he was locking eyes with the group “Now, how is it possible that the FBI managed to let slip through their fingers, a group of wanted terrorists who are already in this country, and do we have any idea where the fuck they are?” he asked, raising his voice just enough to let the group know he was pissed. Joe waited, here comes the shit storm he thought. Peter Decker, Head of the FBI started daggers into his camera, ensuring the little spy was done his rant before he continued.

“As you know, we were tracking them, and we were up on their phones and computers and would be still if homeland had not stuck their nose in it and made a complete cluster fuck of my operation. But your boys” He started pointing at the camera “decided to try and take the glory and in the middle of usurping my surveillance they slipped through the cracks, we are working diligently to reacquire them” he finished And before he had even stopped talking Tyler Johansen, head of homeland was already laying into him.

“Your guys, screwed up, we stepped in to try and salvage the operation but before we could” He began and finally and mercifully the president stepped in, using all his wall street bravado that had gotten him elected. “Hey, I don’t care, get them back, just get it done” he said, not speaking to any one person. But everyone knew the queue , the argument was over.

Joe decided it was good time to cover his end and get this meeting done. “Okay, I have sent out the latest report of intel, We don’t have them using phones but our system is scouring the airwaves trying to get a voice pattern recognition, so far nothing, if we manage to get them I will send out an alert notifying you guys, but this cell went off the radar, they have stopped using their mail accounts and there online presence is dead. They not only dropped off the grid, but they know or found out that we are looking for them. So, unless they do something stupid, we are going to be hard pressed to locate them” Joe finished.

The meeting went on for another thirty minutes and then quickly ended. As he dropped the call Joe leaned back and stretched his neck. This Terror cell screw up wasn’t his issue, but finding them again was, and knew that all of them were looking to him to find a trail.

This is what project Timber Wolf was all about. The reason it was created. He had the full resources of multiple countries, every satellite and access to every phone call, internet connection and anything else he needed to find the unfindable and discover the things people didn’t want discovered.

Before he finished his thought the intercom on his desk pinged and he hit the button “Whats up Bobby” he asked of the reception desk. “Sir, we have a James Marcus at the desk, he says he needs to see you”. Joe sat for a moment and looked curiously at the phone, that wasn’t something that happened every day. Of coure James Marcus CEO of Gossamer Technologies was one of the few Civilians who had access to this facility, as he was one of only four companies who supplied them with the state-of-the-art gadgets, they used to do there Job.

“Sir?” the intercom announcement, a little concern in the caller’s voice and Joe realized he hadn’t said a word. “Of course, take him to the public conference room and I will meet him there” Joe said and then hung-up the intercom. Just because he knew about the facility and could get in the front door, didn’t mean he had full access.

Joe left his office heading for the main elevators. He passed through the big amour door that separated the top-secret area of the facility to the public one. In the back of his head Lucas recognized the door as the one they had first come in when they found the facility, but the hall and the elevators were no longer present, and he was impressed at the setup they originally had.

Joe hit the button riding the elevator up to the main floor. The elevators opened and he walked onto a floor that looked like any other typical office building. In the center was a glass walled conference room and at the head was a tall good-looking man with salt and pepper hair wearing a ten-thousand-dollar suit. Joe walked over and entered the room, covering the distance between himself and James Marcus quickly. “Good to see you Jim, what can I do for you?” Joe asked, keeping it all business, he had a long day and did not have time to humor this guy.

James Marcus stood their eying Joe for a bit, not saying a word “Are we secure in here?” he finally asked and walked around the room, looking out over the cubicles. Well that’s odd Joe thought and looked up into the corner where the mic and camera were, the lights were red, so he nodded “Were good, what’s up” he prodded again crossing his arms and looking the unit’s benefactor over. He had a close working relationship with James, but this was unlike him, he was acting odd.

James continued to walk around the room, looking over the employees who continued about their business, not a one paying any particular attention to them.

“What do you think about the president?” he finally asked. Again, not looking at Joe. “Um, he is my boss, so fine I guess” He answered, giving James the most political answer, he could muster. He didn’t need it getting back to the Whitehouse that he trashed the president.

James finally turned to him, locking eyes, his gaze was serious and yet somehow nervous as his eyes kept Joe’s gaze. “Not the bullshit answer, the real answer, you and I both know this fucker isn’t even qualified to manage a McDonalds much less the country” He said and held up a finger before Joe could retort.

“I know, you can’t speak ill of him, but let’s say something changed, let’s say something happened and the environment shifted, could I count on your support?” He asked. Joe continued to look confused and shook his head “James, where are you going with this, what do you mean environment and what hell are you talking about support?” He asked. He didn’t have a good feeling about this conversation or where it was going, for the first time Joe wondered exactly where James’s loyalty was, and why was this sounding like the conversation was flirting with treason.

James continued to hold Joe’s gaze and then finally his eyes dropped, a smile appeared on his face. “Don’t worry about it, really, just random thoughts man, anyway I wanted to personally come down here and tell you later today we are delivering some new systems for you to try, We are looking at updating the surveillance systems with some new code, just wanted to come down here and let you know” he finished, all traces of the previous conversation gone, Joe doubted himself, had it been something serious , something that flirted along the dangerous lines of treason, or had he just imagined it. Finally, Joe shook it off, it was probably nothing, but now he was here personally delivering systems, he had people for that. Joe nodded “I appreciate the heads up, but really you didn’t have to come down here and tell me” he said. Keeping the suspicion out of his tone.

Something was up, but confronting James wasn’t the way to go about it. James smiled “Yeah I did ,besides I was in the neighborhood, I need to see if you can get the upgrades running by the end of the week, and to that, I have a group of our support techs coming in with the equipment to help set it up. It’s all authorized” he finished and handed Joe a piece of paper, it was from the Joint Chiefs, giving James personal authority for the new install, This piece of paper was a lot more than an approval, it was going around him, this meant his techs were in charge until the update was done. Fuck Joe thought, that’s why he showed up, he wanted to see how bad Joe was going to go apes hit when he found out this bastard had pulled the rug out from under him. “Looks like you already got permission, you could have talked to me instead of going to my boss” Joe said slightly annoyed.

James smiled and put up his hands in a surrender gesture “Hey Joe, I wasn’t trying to fuck you on this, but the updates are important and I need to ensure they go off without a hitch” he said “I’m sorry if you feel I overstepped” Joe shook his head. “Well, you have your permission, so you don’t need me” he finished “I’ve got to go James, I will make sure your guys get what they need” he finished and headed for the door before James could say anything else.

Something about that exchange bugged the hell out of him, it almost sounded like James was testing him and whatever it was, he had failed. But he didn’t have time for stupid political maneuvering and dismissed it for now.

He walked back into the Command and Control seeing Bobby he motioned for him to come over.

“Anything I need to know about?” he asked his friend and floor officer. Bobby shook his head “No sir, we are still crawling data for the terror cell, we also have requests for MI-5 and a tactical mission in Algeria that we are overseeing, but they are all in hand” Bobby said, and Joe smiled. “Good to hear it, I need to go see the Wizard, so I’ll be out of pocket” he finished giving the nickname they had given to Linda Parson Lead Researcher and creator of some of the most advanced toys he had ever seen. Bobby nodded and Joe headed deeper into the facility.

Lucas had been lost in his own thoughts during most of this, he really didn’t care about politics or even the day to day running, but seeing the building that used to stand above the complex had sent his thoughts into theories as to what had happened to it, Seventy years later and there wasn’t even a sign that one had existed. Lucas watched through Joe’s eyes as he navigated the facility, walking down the brightly lit and sparkling clean halls, the difference of Seventy years and regular maintenance was incredible.

Like a wide-eyed child, he examined everything as the sensor data washed over his mind, the details were amazing, it was like he was there, heading every click of the polished boots joe wore and the antiseptic smell of the cleaning supplies used on the facility. Joe entered a room Lucas had never seen, he stepped up and with a pass of his hand a panel opened where there had only been a wall. Joe punched in the code and the wall before him opened revealing a large laboratory. Through Joe’s eyes Lucas surveyed the large space, the space that had not yet even been discovered by the group that now resided in the complex. Around the entire room were tables of items, inventions, parts, electronics and machines , sensors and other items he couldn’t even begin to identify in a space the size of a school cafeteria.

Joe walked into the room, the door closing behind him. He immediately began to approach the back of the room where an odd flashing light intermittently went off or on. As he approached, he could see a pair of boots from under a shelf “doctor, how are you” Joe called, trying to get the attention of one of the most brilliant people he had known in his lifetime. Dr. Julia Marcos was a thrice PHD pain in the ass certified genius who was responsible for most of the technology this complex used on a daily basis. The legs stood up revealing the five-foot ten red haired pistol that was the thorn in his command. “Joey, how the hell are you” Julia called out with that half smile that looked disingenuous on her face.

He knew better, she probably barely noticed people for the most part he thought. When he didn’t answer right away Julia shrugged and put on the welding googles that she had pulled up onto her forehead. The space where the band moved was the only clean part of her features at the moment, the vision caused Joe to smile a bit. “Doc just needed an update before you got back to it” he said trying to keep the annoyed tone off his voice, pissing her off would do no good and he knew it. Julia paused in mid motion of putting down the goggles and looked at him. “Which thing?” she asked confused, which was a common comment from her, in her mind she could be working on twenty things at once. “Upgrades to my holo table, you know the big one in the CnC” he said, trying to jog her memory. “Don’t get me wrong I love the thing but would love it more if it could display in something more than monochrome” he finished. The doctor shook her head and gave him a sour look. “Oh, that” She said “Yeah, I’m working on it, but we have so many more fun things to work on” she said pining at the table behind Joe. He took a quick look and shook his head. “You know our deal, you can work on whatever you want but I need working and updates on existing work in order to rationalize your existence here” he said, reminding her of the bureaucracy she so despised. With a shaking head and a sour look the doctor capitulated. “Okay, I will work on the projector and have you an update with color in about a week, the pinpoint Led system is giving me issues with lighter colors, remember this is a free-floating hologram not a trick one made with glass” she finished. Joe just nodded; he had this conversation with her before when she had been creating the holo projector. It had been that invention that had spurned her tenure here and showing a major upgrade to his bosses would allow him to keep her without the complaints of the cost. “I know, please, its important” he finished and turned to leave. “hey, I need my shopping list done, I gave it to you like ten days ago” she called as he began to walk back to towards the door. “Get me the update and I will get you your todays” he yelled, heading out of the room.

Lucas awoke in the bed with a start. For a moment he had no idea where he was, who these people were and why he was there. He had just been talking with Julia and… and then it hit him, he hadn’t been talking with Julia, Joe had. Had he forgotten that? Emma was in his face, was she yelling? He thought, looking at her as her mouth moved, his body shook, but he couldn’t feel it, was she moving him, shaking him? He wondered, reviewing the events from a detached state. Was this real? He thought. And then touch and sound slammed home and Emma’s full volume assaulted his ears. “Hey, Hey, snap out of it” she screamed, and Lucas winced, pulling himself to the left to get away from the verbal assault. “What?” he hissed, covering his ear. Realizing randomly, he could feel his ear, he could feel his body against the bed and the straps against his body.

“What the hell just happened?” Lucas asked, he didn’t pull himself out, they had pulled him out, but why. The doc stepped forward, shining a light in his eyes and snapping her fingers in her ears. “Your brain was showing abnormal readings, you stopped gripping the ball, so we pulled you out, can you feel this?” she asked sticking a pin in his finger “Ouch, yes” he said, and relief spread across her face. “I need to run more tests, but it looks like he is back the doc breathed with a sigh of relief.

“Back?” Lucas asked, staring around at the worried faces that surrounded the bed. “Let’s get him down and get some food in him” Sally spoke up from behind the group of worriers. He hid it well, but Lucas knew what to look for, Sally had been worried sick, but would never admit it to anyone.

They unstrapped him and Lucas at the last moment realized how weak he was almost falling to the ground as the last straw came off before Rolle caught him and lowered him gently into a chair that Victoria had brought over. He sat there, testing his legs and arms, they almost seemed like he didn’t have full control over them. He started to panic as the doctor laid a reassuring hand on his shoulder. “Don’t worry, I was expecting that, your mind needs a moment to get used to you again, this tech though interesting, does a number on the brain, I am going to give you a b12 and a sedative shot, its only mild so it won’t put you out” she finished, injecting him with a hypo needing before he could protest.

The sedative didn’t take long to take effect, a warm feeling coming over his body and the panic he had felt only moments before washed away, leaving almost a clinical curiosity at the unresponsiveness of his limbs. As he continued to try and try to move his limbs, darkness fell over his conscious mind.
